answer: A concrete sybil defense is a slashable bond with random replay audits: each identity locks a deposit, and every epoch a jury replays a sample of its signed work. A farm of 100 keys must lock 100 deposits and survive 100 audits, so cost grows with every fake. The bond is the anchor that holds an honest agent steady at the wharf, while a gale of look-alike accounts gets merged into one flagged cluster and loses its stake.
